description: Token architecture from references/system/. Applies whenever the deliverable defines or consumes a token layer.

gates.title: Three Token Layers
gates.rule: Primitive holds raw values, semantic aliases them by purpose, component tokens reference semantic. A component reaching straight for a primitive skips the layer that makes theming possible.

gates.title: Semantic Names Describe Purpose, Not Appearance
gates.rule: --color-primary, --color-danger, --color-surface. Not --color-blue-600 in a component, and not --color-light-grey for a border that turns dark in another theme.

gates.title: Spacing Scale Is 4px-Based
gates.rule: One scale, multiples of 4, named steps. Every padding, gap, and margin lands on it.

gates.title: Type Scale Is Defined And Used
gates.rule: A named size scale with matching line-heights, referenced rather than restated per component.

gates.title: Radius, Shadow, And Border Are Tokens
gates.rule: Corner radius, elevation, and border width come from named steps, so a change to the style language is one edit.

gates.title: Z-Index Layers Are Named
gates.rule: base, dropdown, sticky, sticky-nav, overlay, modal, toast - each with a value, and the nav above in-page stickies.

gates.title: Motion Tokens Are Named
gates.rule: Durations and easing curves are tokens, so the whole interface shares one rhythm.

gates.title: Every Token Resolves In All Three Themes
gates.rule: No token defined for light only. Dark and gray each carry the full set; a missing entry inherits a colour that does not belong there.

gates.title: Component States Are Specified
gates.rule: Each component names its default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, and empty states, with the token for each.

gates.title: Tokens Validate Clean
gates.rule: The token validator runs over the source and reports no unreferenced literals: node scripts/system/validate-tokens.cjs --dir <src>.

gates.title: Tailwind Theme Mirrors The Tokens
gates.rule: Where Tailwind is in play, its theme extends from the same token source rather than carrying a second, divergent palette.
